title: Gemini (gemini-3.8-flash-cyber, LiteLLM proxy, RESPONSES wire): MCP tool discovery whose result carries a JSON-Schema $ref. One headless turn: search_tool for the local refprobe MCP fixture (fixtures/refprobe_mcp.py), whose cluster_probe inputSchema uses $defs + "$ref": "#/$defs/cluster_ref" (same shape as the ontap-cluster server's ssh_execute), then use_tool on it. Reproduces the operator-reported Vertex 400 from SCS session 01a179e9-392e-7093-a395-21692e2e9399: 'The referenced name `#/$defs/cluster_ref` in function_response.response does not match to a display_name in the function_response.parts.' Hypothesis under test: the proxy maps the search_tool function_call_output (JSON text) into Gemini function_response.response, and Vertex reads any {"$ref": ...} there as a pointer to a function-response part. Pre-registered red: FAIL (the 400) is the expected evidence before GEM-REF-1; after it, PASS requires the fixture payload in the reply, the use_tool call, the result on the wire and no escaped $ref in any row request (read the verdict from report.md).

steps.prompt: Use the search_tool tool with the query 'cluster probe' to find the refprobe MCP tool, then use the use_tool tool to call refprobe__cluster_probe with arguments cluster 'vsim' and command 'version'. After the tool result is in hand, reply with exactly two lines: line 1: GEM-REF-DONE; line 2: the exact text the tool returned.

ndjson.label: TURN DELIVERED: the reply carries the DONE nonce (the turn survived discovery and the tool call). The nonce is in the prompt, so it only shows the turn finished; payload proves the round trip.

MCP ROUND-TRIP PAYLOAD: the reply quotes the fixture's result text, which is not in the prompt; it can only come from a real use_tool call to refprobe__cluster_probe after a successful discovery turn.

wire.label: CONTROL (premise): the refprobe discovery result reached the row wire. The cluster_ref definition text survives expansion (inside $defs before the fix, inlined at properties.cluster after it), so this pin holds before and after. 0 hits = discovery not exercised (VACUOUS).

FIX PIN: no request to the row carries an escaped \"$ref\" key, i.e. no tool output embedded as a JSON string carries a schema reference (the form Vertex rejects). Tool declarations in tools[] are unescaped and are not matched. Fails before GEM-REF-1, must pass after.

ROUND TRIP ON THE WIRE (call proof): the fixture's result text was sent back to the row as a function_call_output, which only happens after a real use_tool call to refprobe__cluster_probe executed. (An escaped tool-name grep cannot prove the call: the discovery output already carries that name.)

vacuous_if.note: no request carried the refprobe discovery result: the model never ran search_tool for it, so the case says nothing about the $ref defect.
